target.title: Fix retained Amp network sessions
target.body:
## Summary

- Finish every temporary Amp API and dashboard `URLSession` after its request completes or fails.
- Inject session creation/finalization internally so lifecycle behavior is testable without live accounts, cookies, or Keychain access.
- Add serialized regression coverage for API and web fetches across successful responses and transport failures.

## Root cause

Both Amp fetch paths created ephemeral sessions with redirect delegates but never invalidated them. Repeated refreshes could retain delegates, URL-cache state, and transport resources beyond each one-shot request.

target.title: Stop background Claude keychain discovery
target.body:
## Summary

- prevent background MCP-only credential discovery from reading `Claude Code-credentials` through Security.framework when the prompt policy is `onlyOnUserAction`
- preserve MCP-only detection for explicit user refreshes and the opt-in `always` policy
- add regression coverage for both interaction modes

## Root cause

The MCP-only payload detector bypassed the normal Claude prompt-policy gate and issued a Security.framework “no UI” read during background availability checks. Legacy Keychain ACLs can still display the macOS password dialog for these reads, causing recurring prompts even though the call was marked non-interactive.

Fixes #2115.

## User impact

Background refreshes no longer touch the Claude Code Keychain item under the default `onlyOnUserAction` policy. Explicit refreshes can still inspect it when needed.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter ClaudeOAuthCredentialsStoreMCPOnlyGuardTests`
- `make check`
- `make test` *(blocked by an unrelated current-main `AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` baseline failure: “manual mode performs the initial refresh but no recurring ticks” observes 2 refreshes instead of 1; reproduced when running that suite alone)*

No live Keychain read was used for validation.

target.title: Improve DeepSeek detailed usage
target.body: ## Summary - enrich the existing DeepSeek balance with today/current-month cost and token totals, request counts, model/category breakdowns, and a 30-day token chart - discover DeepSeek Platform sessions from Chrome local storage, validate every discovered profile, and offer only valid profiles in Settings - keep the balance and profile selector stable while detailed usage refreshes or a profile changes - scope each profile choice to the active API credential and saved-account slot to prevent cross-account data mixing - bound optional Platform work so a slow or uncooperative browser/session probe cannot delay the required balance ## Why DeepSeek's documented API exposes the account balance but not the detailed usage visible at `platform.deepseek.com/usage`. The Platform dashboard uses private endpoints for that data. This change keeps the documented balance fetch authoritative and required. Platform usage is optional enrichment: failures, invalid sessions, and timeouts preserve the balance instead of failing the provider. ## Compared with #1910 This builds on the same general idea of reading DeepSeek Platform usage, but uses a narrower and more defensive session path: - reads the Platform `userToken` from live Chrome local storage instead of relying on cookies or persisting a manual browser token - discovers all Chrome profiles and validates each session before showing it - lists only valid profiles and requires an explicit choice for a new or changed API credential - fingerprints the API credential/account scope without persisting the credential - keeps imported Platform tokens in memory and logs only opaque profile identifiers - adds hard timeout behavior, profile-catalog preservation, and stable transition presentation Reference: #1910 ## Privacy and reliability - DeepSeek Platform tokens are never written to CodexBar config - legacy DeepSeek `cookieHeader` values are removed during config normalization - private Platform endpoints may change; parser failures degrade to balance-only data - optional session resolution is cancellation-aware and hard-bounded ## Validation - `swift test --filter DeepSeek` — 91 tests passed - `swift test --filter ProviderSettingsDescriptorTests` — 34 tests passed - `make check` — passed with 0 lint violations - `git diff --check` — passed ## UI verification Validated locally with multiple Chrome profiles: - balance remains visible during profile changes - the profile selector remains visible and shows `Refreshing` while disabled - invalid/expired sessions are omitted - detailed usage repopulates after the selected profile refresh completes ## Screenshots

target.title: Fix login-shell probe cleanup
target.body:
## Summary

- Defer login-shell PATH capture until Codex RPC launch, while preserving it for explicit script wrappers such as `#!/usr/bin/env node`.
- Adopt raw `posix_spawn` PATH probes into `SpawnedProcessGroup`, cleaning helpers that escape the original session on timeout and normal exit.
- Prevent cross-probe pipe inheritance with atomic close-on-exec pipes on Linux and a serialized Darwin pipe/spawn boundary using `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT`.
- Add regression coverage for native and script overrides, session-escaped output holders, and close-on-exec descriptors.

## Root cause

The PATH runner only killed the original process group. Shell startup helpers could call `setsid()`, retain a probe output pipe, and survive cleanup. Moving PATH capture later avoided unnecessary work for native overrides, but treating every explicit override alike broke script launchers that depend on login-shell PATH. Pipe descriptors also had a small creation-to-`fcntl` inheritance window when probes overlapped.

## Validation

- `make check`
  - SwiftFormat: 0 files require formatting
  - SwiftLint: 0 violations in 1,428 files
- `make test` through autoreview on fixup commit `ffe09726c`
  - 640/640 selections
  - 54/54 groups passed on first attempt
  - 0 failures, retries, or timeouts
- Post-main-merge exact head `bc40e4bf3`
  - focused resolver/process suite: 80 tests in 6 suites passed
  - `make check`: clean
- Linux portability follow-up keeps atomic `pipe2(O_CLOEXEC)` through a direct glibc/musl symbol declaration after Swift's Linux modules omitted the function declaration.
- Autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings after the portability repair; correctness confidence 0.93.
- Original isolated before/after runtime proof and hashed artifacts: https://gist.github.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/1b3ab2a0f2ee613c442f26e4f72507a7

Screenshots are not applicable because this is subprocess lifecycle behavior.

## Out of scope

The separately observed Codex `auth.json` deletion is unrelated. This patch does not read, write, refresh, or remove Codex authentication state. Validation used isolated homes and test doubles without real account, browser-cookie, or Keychain access.

## Related

- Follow-up to #821
- Builds on terminal isolation work in #2074
- Reproduction: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/821#issuecomment-4957600350

Authored with Claude; maintainer fixups by @steipete.

target.title: feat(diagnostics-otel): add vendor-neutral session attribute option for OTel session grouping
target.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` configuration option that exports a SHA-256 hashed session identifier as three vendor-neutral OTel span attributes on root spans, enabling session grouping across multiple observability backends (Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix, and others).

Fixes #91927
Supersedes #92956 (closed, conflicts)

## Background

The issue originally requested `langfuse.session.id` for Langfuse session grouping. During community discussion, the Latitude team highlighted that session grouping by span attributes is a vendor-neutral convention shared across most OTLP backends. OpenClaw is already moving toward GenAI semantic conventions elsewhere in the exporter, so emitting additional vendor-neutral keys maximizes value across the ecosystem.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw redacts session keys to `"unknown"` in OTel span attributes for security. While this is a reasonable default, it makes observability backends (Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix) unable to aggregate traces by session — the `session.id` attribute on every span is either missing or identical and meaningless. Session grouping is a core feature in every OTLP backend, and without a meaningful session identifier on root spans, users cannot group multi-turn conversations or debug session-level issues.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.base.ts` | Add `sessionAttribute?: boolean` to `DiagnosticsOtelConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.ts` | Add `sessionAttribute: z.boolean().optional()` |
| `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Add help text for `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` |
| `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Add field label for `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` | Emit hashed session ID on `openclaw.run` and `openclaw.harness.run` root spans |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` | 2 test cases (enabled + disabled), 97 total passing |
| `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` | Document session attribute, privacy model, and opt-in guidance |

## Vendor-Neutral Attributes

When `sessionAttribute: true` is set, all three attributes are emitted with the same SHA-256 hash value:

- **`langfuse.session.id`** — Langfuse compatibility
- **`session.id`** — OpenInference / Arize de-facto standard
- **`gen_ai.conversation.id`** — GenAI semantic conventions

This ensures session grouping works across Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix, and any OTLP backend without requiring backends to map non-standard keys.

## Security

- **Opt-in only** (default: `false`) — current redaction posture is unchanged
- **SHA-256 hash**, never the raw `agent:platform:peer` key
- Raw `openclaw.sessionKey` stays redacted as `"unknown"` in all existing paths
- The session identifier never leaves the box unless the operator explicitly opts in

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed:** Add opt-in `sessionAttribute` config to export hashed session identifiers on root spans.

**Real environment tested:**
- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- Runtime: Node v24.3.0, pnpm 11.2.2
- Setup: OpenClaw local dev instance, diagnostics-otel extension

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
1. Added `sessionAttribute?: boolean` to `DiagnosticsOtelConfig` type and Zod schema
2. On `harness.run.started` and `run.started` events, compute `crypto.createHash("sha256")` of `sessionKey` and emit three vendor-neutral attributes
3. Raw `openclaw.sessionKey` remains in the redaction set — never exposed
4. Ran reproduction script and full test suite for diagnostics-otel

**Evidence after fix (reproduction output):**
```
========================================================================
=== OpenClaw diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute — Reproduction ===
========================================================================

--- 1. Input ---
  sessionKey:          agent:main:slack:channel:C01ABCDEFG

--- 2. SHA-256 Hash (applied in service.ts) ---
  SHA-256 hash:        6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  Hash length:         64 hex chars (256 bits)

--- 3. OTel Span Attributes Emitted ---
  langfuse.session.id        = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  session.id                 = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  gen_ai.conversation.id     = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0

--- 4. Security Verification ---
  Raw key embedded in hash?  ✅ NO
  sessionAttribute default:  false (opt-in only)
  openclaw.sessionKey:       remains redacted as "unknown"

--- 5. Root Span Attributes (OTLP format) ---
{
  "openclaw.harness.id": "codex",
  "openclaw.provider": "openai",
  "openclaw.model": "gpt-5.4",
  "openclaw.channel": "qa",
  "langfuse.session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "gen_ai.conversation.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0"
}

--- 6. Verification ---
  ✅ SHA-256 hash is irreversible — raw key not recoverable
  ✅ All three vendor-neutral attributes emitted
  ✅ sessionAttribute is opt-in (default: false)
  ✅ No raw session key in exported attributes

========================================================================
Reproduction complete — real behavior demonstrated.
```

**Test suite output:**
```
 RUN  v4.1.7 /home/0668001202/workspace/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  97 passed (97)
   Start at  12:33
   Duration  6.45s
```

**Observed result after the fix:**

Without the fix, OTel spans have no session identifier — `session.id` is missing from root spans, and backends cannot group traces by session.

With the fix and `sessionAttribute: true`:
```
root span attributes: {
  "langfuse.session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "gen_ai.conversation.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  ...
}
```

**What was not tested:** N/A

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Unit Tests | ✅ | 97/97 passed (2 new sessionAttribute tests) |
| Type Check | ✅ | No errors (full project `tsc --noEmit`) |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`) — **No** (opt-in, default-off preserves existing behavior)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No` — backward compatible, `sessionAttribute` is optional with safe default `undefined`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No` — raw session key remains redacted, SHA-256 hash is irreversible, opt-in only)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The new config key is purely additive with a safe default (`undefined` = current behavior)

How is that risk mitigated?
- Default-off preserves existing behavior for all users
- Only a SHA-256 hash (not the raw key) is exported
- Full test coverage for both enabled and disabled states
- Schema help and docs explain the privacy model
